Annexure-II Terms & Conditions of Contract 1. SCOPE OF WORK: Rectification work of Soil Settlement and Sinking of Fo undations by Cementitious Pressure Grouting Method (Soil Stabilization thro ugh lime treatment) in 400KV Switchyard at Kudgi GIS Substation. Any special tools / consumables required for the work shall be under the sco pe of contractor. 2. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION: The work should be executed as detailed in BoQ. The vendor shall ensure th at all SOP is detailed below is to be followed. STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE (SOP) FOR LIME-CEMENT SLURRY SOIL S TABILIZATION: i. Material Selection Binders: Use commercially available hydrated lime / quick lime (conforming t o IS 712) and OPC 43/53 Grade cement. Additives: Water and optional Bentonite powder “optional” (2-4% of binder weight) to improve suspension stability. ii. Site Preparation Marking and Clearing: Mark the stabilization area and remove any surface gr avel. Drilling: Drill holes (35-75 mm diameter) at 450mm to 600mm c/c to a minim um depth of 3 meters using a mechanical rig or manual auger. Drainage: Ensure proper drainage to prevent water pooling. iii. Slurry Preparation Mixing: Combine equal amount of hydrated / quick lime with equal amount of OPC cement and mix it with water. Consistency: Use a blender for 3 to 5 minutes until the slurry is uniform an d lump-free. Density: The expected slurry density should be 1.55-1.65 g/cc. iv. Application (Pressure Injection)

Method: Use a mechanized rig to pressure inject the slurry into drilled holes through a perforated grout pipe, injecting from the bottom upwards. Pressure: Maintain pressure between 0.2 MPa and 0.5 MPa (maximum 0.7 MPa) to avoid surface heave or foundation uplift. Timing: Inject the slurry immediately after mixing (within a few minutes) to prevent settling or hardening Termination: Stop grouting if pressure rises sharply, grout consumption dro ps, surface heave exceeds 2-3 mm, or grout emerges from adjacent holes. v. Mellowing and Compaction Mellowing: Allow a period of 24 to 48 hours for chemical reactions (cation e xchange and flocculation) to occur. Compaction: Perform final surface compaction by mechanical or manual m eans after the mellowing period. vi. Curing and Protection Duration: Cure the area for 7 days by maintaining moisture through light sp rinkling. Protection: Protect the site from extreme weather and avoid major movemen t or activity during the curing phase. Reaction Period: Note that full chemical reactions and strength gains conti nue for 21-45 days. Grouting is an essential ground improvement technique that can considerabl y enhance soil strength and stability. It involves the injection of cement slurr y grout with expansive chemical into the soil to fill voids, compact the groun d, and mitigate soil settlement. ➢ Inspection of site to determine number & location of grouting. ➢ Preliminary preparation of surface for Grouting. ➢ Drilling of the hole to required depth. ➢ Injecting the lime & cement slurry through pressure grouting machine to fi ll the voids. ➢ Filling the Drilled hole with same grouting material after completion of Gro uting. ➢ Above scope of work inclusive of all material, machineries, labours & along with 5 bags of cement & 5bags of consumption total up to 10 bags per footin g. Any additional cement required beyond 10 bags (5 bags cement + 5 bags lime) per footing shall be charged separately on a per-bag basis. Cement Rs. 350/- per 50kg bag, lime Rs.1,250/- per 50kg bag ➢ Arrangement for water & Single & three-Phase power at the workplace to be facilitated by the client. SCOPE OF WORK: Rectification work of Soil Settlement and Sinking of Fo undations by Cementitious Pressure Grouting Method (Soil Stabilization thro ugh lime treatment) in 400KV Switchyard at Kudgi GIS Substation. Any special tools / consumables required for the work shall be under the sco pe of contractor. 2. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION: The work should be executed as detailed in BoQ. The vendor shall ensure th at all SOP is detailed below is to be followed. STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE (SOP) FOR LIME-CEMENT SLURRY SOIL S TABILIZATION: i. Material Selection Binders: Use commercially available hydrated lime / quick lime (conforming t o IS 712) and OPC 43/53 Grade cement. Additives: Water and optional Bentonite powder “optional” (2-4% of binder weight) to improve suspension stability. ii. Site Preparation Marking and Clearing: Mark the stabilization area and remove any surface gr avel. Drilling: Drill holes (35-75 mm diameter) at 450mm to 600mm c/c to a minim um depth of 3 meters using a mechanical rig or manual auger. Drainage: Ensure proper drainage to prevent water pooling. iii. Slurry Preparation Mixing: Combine equal amount of hydrated / quick lime with equal amount of OPC cement and mix it with water. Consistency: Use a blender for 3 to 5 minutes until the slurry is uniform an d lump-free. Density: The expected slurry density should be 1.55-1.65 g/cc. iv. Application (Pressure Injection)

Method: Use a mechanized rig to pressure inject the slurry into drilled holes through a perforated grout pipe, injecting from the bottom upwards. Pressure: Maintain pressure between 0.2 MPa and 0.5 MPa (maximum 0.7 MPa) to avoid surface heave or foundation uplift. Timing: Inject the slurry immediately after mixing (within a few minutes) to prevent settling or hardening Termination: Stop grouting if pressure rises sharply, grout consumption dro ps, surface heave exceeds 2-3 mm, or grout emerges from adjacent holes. v. Mellowing and Compaction Mellowing: Allow a period of 24 to 48 hours for chemical reactions (cation e xchange and flocculation) to occur. Compaction: Perform final surface compaction by mechanical or manual m eans after the mellowing period. vi. Curing and Protection Duration: Cure the area for 7 days by maintaining moisture through light sp rinkling. Protection: Protect the site from extreme weather and avoid major movemen t or activity during the curing phase. Reaction Period: Note that full chemical reactions and strength gains conti nue for 21-45 days. Grouting is an essential ground improvement technique that can considerabl y enhance soil strength and stability. It involves the injection of cement slurr y grout with expansive chemical into the soil to fill voids, compact the groun d, and mitigate soil settlement. ➢ Inspection of site to determine number & location of grouting. ➢ Preliminary preparation of surface for Grouting. ➢ Drilling of the hole to required depth. ➢ Injecting the lime & cement slurry through pressure grouting machine to fi ll the voids. ➢ Filling the Drilled hole with same grouting material after completion of Gro uting. ➢ Above scope of work inclusive of all material, machineries, labours & along with 5 bags of cement & 5bags of consumption total up to 10 bags per footin g.
